literature_notes: Three ledger lines were evaluated. L1 and L2 (PMC9588774) describe the same construct: full-length CD95/FAS with an HA signal peptide swapped in at the N-terminus and a FLAG/hexahistidine tag appended at the C-terminus. The HA sequence is part of the signal peptide and is cleaved co-translationally — it never reaches the cell surface. The FLAG/His tag is at the intracellular C-terminus (FAS is a type I single-pass receptor; residues 191–335 are cytoplasmic). Neither position qualifies as an extracellular surface tag site. L3 (PMC12217004) reports a myc-tag inserted into the full extracellular domain of membrane-bound FasL (CD95 Ligand / TNFSF6), which is the cognate ligand of FAS, not FAS itself (CD95 / TNFRSF6). These are distinct proteins; a tag in FasL's ECD provides no positional precedent for a tag in FAS. No ledger line supports an extracellular surface tag on FAS at any residue or loop. Zero sites is the correct answer.

literature_other_positions.note: FLAG/hexahistidine tag appended at the C-terminus of full-length CD95; FAS is a type I transmembrane protein whose C-terminus (residues 191–335) is entirely intracellular — this is a cytoplasmic tag, not a surface tag.
